correctness.rationale: For fixed a>b>0 and q in (0,1), substituting t=s exp(-z) gives lower minus upper mass of g(t)=exp(-bt)-exp(-at). Its log-elasticity E(t)=-bt+(a-b)t/(exp((a-b)t)-1) strictly decreases on t>0. Differentiating the log lower/upper mass ratio with respect to log s gives the difference of two positive-weight means of E on ordered intervals; the difference is strictly positive, since the shared endpoint has measure zero. At s down to 0 the ratio tends to q^2; at infinity it is asymptotic to exp(b(q-q^2)s), by direct integration of the leading exponential. This establishes one crossing with the stated orientation for every allowed triple. For small L the gap divided by L^2 tends at each fixed s to -s g(s)(1+E(s)), changing sign at the unique mode of s g(s). In the thick limit the substitution y=qs gives the difference from the two half-line masses at y, with a unique median. In each case opposite signs at fixed bracketing values force convergence of the unique roots. The integrated formulas and signed rational witnesses agree; independent bisection gives s_c=2.802054039187418 and productivities 0.2077660717709528 and 0.1130205774372200 in the frozen example. value.rationale: Equal optical-depth treatments isolate differential inhibition from differential shading. Even pointwise productivity domination does not tell which ordering is preferable; the unique crossover and its mode-versus-median endpoint laws give exact guidance for this natural two-stratum benchmark across all inhibition contrasts, not just numerical examples. This is a model-level result, not an agronomic recommendation.
